title: Profiling playbook: GPU hotfix repro & Nsight capture steps
body:
Purpose:
This is a concise playbook for reproducing and capturing the GPU occupancy regression that surfaced after the recent runtime hotfix (PR #892). The goal is not only to reproduce reliably on an internal test cluster but to collect a minimal yet high-signal Nsight trace and CUDA-graph capture so we can debug kernel handoff timing, async copies, and stream scheduling differences introduced by the change.

Scope / observed symptom recap:
- Regression: 10–30% drop in effective SM occupancy and ~15–45ms tail-latency increase on 8xA100 dedicated nodes for the small-batch chat endpoint.
- Affected path: decoder-only generation with KV cache enabled, frequent short requests (seq_len 16–64), microbatching enabled at the inference layer.
- Hotfix candidate: reordered kernel launch sequence in stream-manager to prioritize completion callbacks earlier (intended to reduce latency for long sequences).
- Variance: Repro is flaky on dev boxes unless we match production batch inter-arrival jitter and the same CUDA/cuDNN versions.

Quick checklist (what to run locally first)
1) Match env: use the same driver/cuda/cuDNN versions as prod (documented in linked_artifacts).
2) Use dedicated test GPU (8xA100 profile equivalence preferred) or the infra emulation script run_on_prod_like.sh.
3) Small synthetic harness: run the request-replay harness with the exact request arrival pattern (replay file: reproducer/replay/kv_shortseq_2026-07.json).
4) Confirm baseline: run without hotfix (checkout commit before PR #892) then with hotfix. Record occupancy metrics from our internal exporter.

Nsight capture recipe (minimal high-signal settings)
- Tool: nsight systems (nsys) for timeline + kernel launch ordering, and nsight compute (ncu) for per-kernel counters when needed.
- nsys capture (timeline):
  nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --output=nsys/capture-hotfix-repro \
    --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --force-overwrite 
    --env NVTX_STACK_COLLECT=1 -- 
    ./inference_harness --replay reproducer/kv_shortseq_2026-07.json --workers 8
  Notes: use --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi and instrument around the exact request window to reduce noise.
- ncu capture (per-kernel stats):
  ncu --metrics "sm__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed,sm__active_cycles.avg,dram__throughput.avg" \
    --target-processes all --set full --output ncu/hotfix-kernels ./inference_harness ...
  Notes: only run ncu after you have isolated the problematic kernel list from the nsys timeline to keep overhead low.

CUDA-graph capture variant (important because our runtime uses cudaGraphInstantiate in steady-state):
- Environment variable to force graph capture on for a short window: REDWOOD_FORCE_GRAPH_ON=1 REDWOOD_GRAPH_WINDOW=20
- Capture two runs: (A) graph mode disabled, (B) graph mode enabled. Compare launch counts and trace differences.
- Use the runtime flag to serialise graph instantiation logs: --dump-cudagraph-walk A (writes summary to /tmp/cudagraph-walk.json).

Which timelines to inspect in nsys (high priority)
- Stream lanes: look for gaps between memcpyAsync (H2D / D2H) and kernel launches on the decoder stream.
- Kernel launch density: identify long idle pockets on compute streams; look for 'launch' spikes on host side followed by quiet on GPU.
- NVTX ranges: ensure we have ranges for batch boundaries, kv-prefetch start/end, and cudaGraph instantiate points.
- OS interactions: check process preemption and CPU-side queuing that may create delayed kernel submission.

Key counters to collect (ncu / perf API names we check)
- sm__active_cycles.avg: how much time SMs are doing something
- sm__inst_executed.per_cycle_active: instruction throughput per active cycle
- sm__warps_active.avg.per_cycle_active: warp occupancy indicator
- sm__inst_issued.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed: IPC proxy
- l1tex__t_sectors_yielded_pipe_lsu_mem_global_ops_mem_shared_ld: rough L1 behavior (optional)
- dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed: DRAM saturation

Hypotheses to test (with experiment pairs)
1) Hand-off reordering introduced micro-gap jitter: the hotfix moves completion callbacks earlier which causes earlier stream barrier/priority swaps and leaves small windows without prefetched KV pages. Test: revert ordering and compare gap histogram (nsys timeline).
2) CUDA graph instantiation timing changed: more frequent graph re-instantiations increase host-side CPU work and serialize launches. Test: force graph mode on/off and correlate host-side CPU usage in nsys.
3) Async copy phasing: prefetch window decreased relative to kernel start, causing more frequent waiting for H2D. Test: instrument async copy NVTX ranges and check memcpy->kernel latency distribution.
4) Stream priority interactions: the new callback ordering causes compute kernels to be enqueued on a lower-priority stream after helper kernels, increasing preemption. Test: capture stream IDs in timeline and vary stream priority config.

Repro run matrix (short version)
- Sequence lengths: 16, 32, 64
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8
- Microbatch: on/off
- Graph mode: on/off
- Prefetch window: default, +25ms, +50ms
- Repeat each cell 10 times and collect median + p95 of occupancy and latency.

Quick parsing heuristics (when skimming traces)
- Occupancy drop pattern: if occupancy drops mostly at start-of-request -> suspect prefetch/KV. If drop spreads across timeline -> suspect kernel inefficiency.
- Host idle spikes followed by kernel burst -> host-side serialization (graph/instantiate).
- Many short memcpy calls in tight alternation with kernels -> take a closer look at async-copy alignment and CUDA stream dependencies.

Immediate mitigations to try (low-risk)
- Increase KV prefetch window by +25ms in config and re-run repro. If occupancy recovers, we have a strong signal.
- Pin critical kernel launches to a high-priority stream as a temporary workaround.
- Disable the hotfix reorder behind a runtime flag and roll it out to a canary.

Longer-term investigative tasks
- Add histogram telemetry to exporter: async-copy->kernel latency distribution, cudaGraph instantiate frequency, and per-request host CPU blocking time.
- Add a small microbenchmark harness that reproduces only the launch-ordering pattern to iterate faster (no network, small in-memory model).
- Schedule a deep-dive with HW team if ncu counters show low IPC with high DRAM utilization (possible memory-bound behavior).

Notes & gotchas seen in past captures:
- Nsight on multi-GPU nodes will collapse stream ids; always capture per-process and include GPU indices in filenames.
- ncu metric sets can change across driver versions; pin versions and keep a small copy of the exact ncu command output used for comparison.
- High-resolution traces are large; use targeted capture windows and offload to the profiling S3 bucket immediately.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: run baseline vs hotfix matrix on qa-prod-8x (scrips + upload traces) (ETA 2026-07-16).
- Marco: prepare ncu metric list and run per-kernel sampling for the top 8 kernels (ETA 2026-07-18).
- Daniel: add quick exporter histograms for async-copy->kernel latency (ETA 2026-07-23).
- Sofia: evaluate temporary runtime flag to revert launch-ordering and run a canary (ETA 2026-07-19).

Appendix: quick commands (copyable)
- Start nsys: nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --output=/tmp/nsys-hotfix --trace=cuda,osrt --force-overwrite -- ./bin/inference_harness --replay replay.json
- Short ncu: ncu --metrics sm__active_cycles.avg,sm__inst_issued.avg,pct,dram__throughput.avg --target-processes all --output /tmp/ncu-hotfix ./bin/inference_harness --replay replay.json

If you hit a blocking Nsight issue (hang, missing kernels), add --capture-range=process and reduce the runtime window by instrumenting NVTX ranges in code. Keep raw traces in /profiling/2026-07/hotfix-repro and add short README with run parameters.

If you find a clear signal (e.g., prefetch gap is root cause), dump a minimal repro harness and open JIRA-ENG-4572 with the artifacts and suggested rollback.

End of playbook.
